key_insight: Local gating sharply reduces spectral bias in L² regression, but H¹ energy losses retain Θ(N²) conditioning and require preconditioning.
engineering_relevance: For mechanics surrogates, local architectures can balance regression learning rates, but variational or physics-informed training may still need operator-aware preconditioning.
method: Multiply shallow ReLU features by hat partition-of-unity weights.
Analyze learning rates through Gram-matrix eigenvalues and block-Toeplitz symbols.
Use an interior-stencil preconditioner to address H¹ spectral bias.
evidence_signal: In 1D regression, the measured learning-rate spread falls from 1.9×10⁵ to 4.5 at matched model size; Poisson experiments confirm the contrasting H¹ behavior.
watch_item: The main theory concerns shallow models linear in trainable parameters; evidence for training hidden-layer parameters is limited to regression experiments.
paper_title: Spectral Bias Reduction in Local Gated ReLU Architectures
